sentences.zh: 天祐九年春正月庚辰朔，周德威等自飛狐東下。

translations.literal: In spring of Tianyou 9, first month, first day gengchen, Zhou Dewei and others marched east from Feihu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of Tianyou 9 (gengchen new moon), Zhou Dewei led his force east from Feihu.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，會鎮、定之師進營祁溝。

translations.literal: On bingxu the armies of Zhen and Ding united and advanced to camp at Qigou.
translations.idiomatic: On bingxu the Zhen and Ding columns joined and encamped at Qigou.

sentences.zh: 庚子，次涿州，刺史劉知溫以城歸順。

translations.literal: On gengzi they halted at Zhuozhou; prefect Liu Zhiwen surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi they reached Zhuozhou, where Prefect Liu Zhiwen opened the gates.

sentences.zh: 德威進迫幽州，守光出兵拒戰，燕將王行方等以部下四百人來奔。

translations.literal: Dewei pressed toward Youzhou; Shouguang led troops to resist; Yan generals Wang Xingfang and others with four hundred followers came over.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei closed on Youzhou; Shouguang marched out to fight, while Yan officers including Wang Xingfang defected with four hundred men.

sentences.zh: 二月庚戌朔，梁祖大舉河南之眾以援守光，以陝州節度使楊師厚為招討使，河南李周彝為副；

translations.literal: Second month, first day gengxu, the Liang Founder raised all the Henan host to relieve Shouguang, appointing Shaanxi military commissioner Yang Shihou campaign commander and Henan's Li Zhouyi deputy;
translations.idiomatic: On the gengxu new moon of the second month the Liang Founder mobilized Henan to save Shouguang, naming Yang Shihou of Shaanxi commander and Li Zhouyi of Henan his deputy;

sentences.zh: 青州賀德倫為應接使，鄆州袁象先為副。

translations.literal: Qingzhou's He Delun liaison commander, and Yanzhou's Yuan Xiangxian deputy.
translations.idiomatic: with He Delun of Qingzhou as liaison commander and Yuan Xiangxian of Yanzhou as his deputy.

sentences.zh: 甲子，梁祖自洛陽趨魏州，遣楊師厚、李周彝攻鎮州之棗強，命賀德倫攻蓚縣。

translations.literal: On jiazi the Liang Founder left Luoyang for Weizhou, sent Yang Shihou and Li Zhouyi to attack Zaoqiang in Zhen prefecture, and ordered He Delun to attack Shuo county.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he quit Luoyang for Weizhou, sent Yang Shihou and Li Zhouyi against Zaoqiang in Zhen, and ordered He Delun on Shuo county.

sentences.zh: 三月壬午，梁祖自督軍攻棗強。

translations.literal: Third month, renwu, the Liang Founder personally supervised the attack on Zaoqiang.
translations.idiomatic: On renwu in the third month the Liang Founder took personal command at Zaoqiang.

sentences.zh: 甲申，城陷，屠之。

translations.literal: On jiashen the city fell and was put to the sword.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen the city was taken and massacred.

sentences.zh: 時李存審與史建瑭以三千騎屯趙州，相與謀曰：「梁軍若不攻蓚城，必西攻深、冀。

translations.literal: At that time Li Cunshen and Shi Jiantang with three thousand horse were stationed at Zhao prefecture; they consulted together and said: "If the Liang army does not attack Shuo city, it will surely strike west at Shen and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunshen and Shi Jiantang held Zhao with three thousand cavalry and agreed: "If Liang skips Shuo, it will drive on Shen and Ji.

sentences.zh: 吾王方北伐，以南鄙之事付我輩，豈可坐觀其弊。

translations.literal: Our lord is on the northern campaign and has left the southern frontier to us—how can we sit and watch him suffer harm?
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu is campaigning north and trusted the south to us—we cannot stand by while he is hurt.

sentences.zh: 」乃以八百騎趨冀州，扼下博橋，令史建瑭、李都督分道擒生。

translations.literal: " They then took eight hundred horse toward Ji prefecture, seized Xiabo Bridge, and ordered Shi Jiantang and Commander Li to take captives by separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: They took eight hundred horse to Ji, held Xiabo Bridge, and sent Shi Jiantang and Commander Li to seize prisoners on separate paths.

sentences.zh: 翌日，諸軍皆至，獲芻牧者數百人，盡殺之；

translations.literal: Next day all units arrived; several hundred hay-cutters and herders were taken and all were killed;
translations.idiomatic: The next day the detachments united, seized several hundred foragers, and killed them all;

sentences.zh: 縱數人逸去，且告：「晉王至矣。

translations.literal: A few were let go and told: "The Prince of Jin has come.
translations.idiomatic: a few were released to spread word that "the Prince of Jin has arrived."

sentences.zh: 」建瑭與李都督各領百餘騎，旗幟軍號類梁軍，與芻牧者雜行，暮及賀德倫營門，殺守門者，縱火大呼，俘斬而旋。

translations.literal: " Jiantang and Commander Li each led a hundred-odd horse with flags and army signals like the Liang army, mingled with the foragers, and at dusk reached He Delun's camp gate, killed the gate guards, set fire and shouted, then took captives and heads and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jiantang and Commander Li each led a little over a hundred horsemen with Liang-style banners and signals, mixed with the foragers, struck He Delun's gate at dusk, killed the guards, fired the camp, and withdrew with prisoners and heads.

sentences.zh: 又執芻牧者，斷其手，令回，梁軍乃夜遁。

translations.literal: They again seized foragers, cut off their hands, and sent them back; the Liang army then fled by night.
translations.idiomatic: They maimed more captives and sent them back, and the Liang force fled in the night.

sentences.zh: 蓚人持鋤耰白梃追擊之，悉獲其輜重。

translations.literal: Shuo men with hoes, mattocks, and white staves pursued and recovered all their baggage train.
translations.idiomatic: Peasants of Shuo chased them with hoes, flails, and clubs and recovered the entire train.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《通鑒·後梁紀》云：帝燒營夜遁，迷失道，委曲行百五十里。

translations.literal: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror · Annals of Later Liang》 says: The Emperor burned his camp and fled by night, lost the road, and wound about one hundred fifty li.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Comprehensive Mirror · Annals of Later Liang》 records that the Liang emperor burned camp and fled by night, lost the road, and wandered one hundred fifty li.

sentences.zh: 戊子旦，乃至冀州。

translations.literal: At dawn on wuzi he finally reached Ji prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn on wuzi he reached Ji prefecture.

sentences.zh: 蓚之耕者皆荷鋤奮挺逐之，委棄軍資器械，不可勝計。）〉

translations.literal: Shuo farmers all shouldered hoes and brandished staves in pursuit; abandoned supplies and weapons were beyond counting.)〉
translations.idiomatic: Farmers of Shuo pursued with hoes and clubs, leaving supplies and arms heaped beyond count.)〉

sentences.zh: 梁祖聞之大駭，自棗強馳歸貝州，殺其將張正言、許從實、朱彥柔，以其亡師於蓚故也。

translations.literal: The Liang Founder was greatly alarmed on hearing it; he galloped from Zaoqiang back to Beizhou and executed his generals Zhang Zhengyan, Xu Congshi, and Zhu Yanrou because they had lost the army at Shuo.
translations.idiomatic: The news terrified the Liang Founder; he raced from Zaoqiang to Beizhou and executed Zhang Zhengyan, Xu Congshi, and Zhu Yanrou for the defeat at Shuo.

sentences.zh: 梁祖先抱痼疾，因是愈甚。

translations.literal: The Liang Founder had long suffered a chronic illness, and from this it grew worse.
translations.idiomatic: His chronic illness, already grave, now worsened.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，滄州都將張萬進殺留後劉繼威，自為滄帥，遣人送款於梁，亦乞降於帝。

translations.literal: On xinchou Cangzhou garrison commander Zhang Wanjin killed the acting prefect Liu Jiwei and made himself Cang commander; he sent envoys to submit to Liang and also begged surrender from the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou Zhang Wanjin of Cangzhou killed Acting Prefect Liu Jiwei, took command, sent allegiance to Liang, and asked Cunxu for terms as well.

sentences.zh: 戊申，周德威遣李存暉攻瓦橋關，下之。

translations.literal: On wushen Zhou Dewei sent Li Cunhui to attack Waqiao Pass and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Zhou Dewei sent Li Cunhui against Waqiao Pass and captured it.

sentences.zh: 四月丁巳，梁祖自魏南歸，疾篤故也。

translations.literal: Fourth month, dingsi, the Liang Founder returned south from Wei because his illness was severe.
translations.idiomatic: On dingsi in the fourth month the Liang Founder withdrew south from Wei, his illness critical.

sentences.zh: 戊申，李嗣源攻瀛州，拔之。

translations.literal: On wushen Li Siyuan attacked Ying prefecture and took it.
translations.idiomatic: On wushen Li Siyuan stormed Ying prefecture and seized it.

sentences.zh: 五月乙卯朔，周德威大破燕軍於羊頭岡，擒大將單廷珪，斬首五千餘級。

translations.literal: Fifth month, first day yimao, Zhou Dewei routed the Yan army at Yangtou Ridge, captured great general Shan Tinggui, and beheaded more than five thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On the yimao new moon of the fifth month Zhou Dewei smashed the Yan host at Yangtou Ridge, took the great general Shan Tinggui, and beheaded over five thousand.

sentences.zh: 德威自涿州進軍於幽州，營於城下。

translations.literal: Dewei advanced from Zhuozhou on Youzhou and camped below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei marched from Zhuozhou to Youzhou and pitched camp under the walls.

sentences.zh: 閏月己酉，攻其西門，燕人出戰，敗之。

translations.literal: Intercalary month, jiyou, they attacked the west gate; the Yan men came out to fight and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou in the intercalary month they assaulted the west gate; the Yan sortie was beaten.

sentences.zh: 六月戊寅，梁祖為其子友珪所弑，友珪僭即帝位於洛陽。

translations.literal: Sixth month, wuyin, the Liang Founder was murdered by his son Yougui, who usurped the throne at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: On wuyin in the sixth month the Liang Founder was killed by his son Yougui, who seized the throne at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 秋八月，朱友珪遣其將韓、康懷英、牛存節率兵五萬，急攻河中。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, Zhu Yougui sent his generals Han, Kang Huaiying, and Niu Cunjie with fifty thousand troops to press the attack on Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn Zhu Yougui sent Han Gong, Kang Huaiying, and Niu Cunjie with fifty thousand men in a furious siege of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 朱友謙遣使來求援，帝命李存審率師救之。

translations.literal: Zhu Youqian sent envoys begging aid; the Emperor ordered Li Cunshen to lead troops to rescue.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youqian asked for help, and Cunxu ordered Li Cunshen to the relief.

sentences.zh: 十月癸未，帝自澤州路赴河中，遇梁將康懷英於平陽，破之，斬首千餘級，追至白徑嶺。

translations.literal: Tenth month, guiwei, the Emperor went to Hezhong by the Zezhou route, met Liang general Kang Huaiying at Pingyang, defeated him, beheaded more than a thousand, and pursued to Baijing Ridge.
translations.idiomatic: On guiwei in the tenth month Cunxu marched on Hezhong by way of Ze, met Kang Huaiying at Pingyang, routed him, took a thousand heads, and chased him to Baijing Ridge.

sentences.zh: 朱友謙會帝於猗氏，梁軍解圍而去。

translations.literal: Zhu Youqian joined the Emperor at Yishi; the Liang army lifted the siege and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Youqian met Cunxu at Yishi, and the Liang besiegers broke off and left.

sentences.zh: 庚申，周德威報劉守光三遣使乞和，不報。

translations.literal: On gengshen Zhou Dewei reported that Liu Shouguang had thrice sent envoys begging peace and received no answer.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen Zhou Dewei reported that Liu Shouguang had sued for peace three times without reply.

sentences.zh: 丁卯，燕將趙行實來奔。

translations.literal: On dingmao Yan general Zhao Xingshi came over.
translations.idiomatic: On dingmao the Yan officer Zhao Xingshi defected.

sentences.zh: 三月甲辰朔，收盧台軍。

translations.literal: Third month, first day jiachen, the Lutai army was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On the jiachen new moon of the third month the Lutai garrison was secured.

sentences.zh: 乙丑，收古北口。

translations.literal: On yichou Gubeikou was taken.
translations.idiomatic: On yichou Gubeikou fell.

sentences.zh: 時居庸關使胡令珪等與諸戍將相繼挈族來奔。

translations.literal: At that time Juyong Pass commissioner Hu Linggui and the frontier garrison commanders in succession brought their clans and came over.
translations.idiomatic: Juyong commissioner Hu Linggui and one frontier commander after another fled in with their families.

sentences.zh: 丙寅，武州刺史高行珪遣使乞降。

translations.literal: On bingyin Wu prefecture commissioner Gao Xinggui sent envoys begging surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On bingyin Gao Xinggui of Wu prefecture sent envoys offering surrender.

sentences.zh: 時劉守光遣愛將元行欽收馬於山北，聞行珪有變，率戍兵攻行珪，行珪遣其弟行溫為質，且乞應援。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Shouguang had sent his favorite general Yuan Xingqin to gather horses north of the mountains; hearing of Xinggui's defection, he led garrison troops to attack Xinggui; Xinggui sent his younger brother Xingwen as hostage and also begged for reinforcements.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Shouguang had sent Yuan Xingqin to round up horses in the northern hills; when Xinggui turned, Xingqin attacked with the garrison, so Xinggui gave his brother Xingwen as hostage and pleaded for aid.

sentences.zh: 周德威遣李嗣源、李嗣本、安金全率兵救武州，降元行欽以歸。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei sent Li Siyuan, Li Siben, and An Jinquan with troops to rescue Wu prefecture and brought Yuan Xingqin back in surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei sent Li Siyuan, Li Siben, and An Jinquan to relieve Wu and returned with Yuan Xingqin as a captive.

sentences.zh: 四月甲申，燕將李暉等二十餘人舉族來奔。

translations.literal: Fourth month, jiashen, more than twenty Yan officers including Li Hui came over with their clans.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen in the fourth month over twenty Yan officers led by Li Hui defected with their families.

sentences.zh: 德威攻幽州南門。

translations.literal: Dewei attacked Youzhou's south gate.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei assaulted the south gate of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，劉守光遣使王遵化致書哀祈於德威，德威戲遵化曰：「大燕皇帝尚未郊天，何怯劣如是耶！

translations.literal: On renchen Liu Shouguang sent envoy Wang Zunhua with a letter of tearful plea to Dewei; Dewei jested to Zunhua: "The Great Yan emperor has not yet performed the suburban sacrifice—why so timid!
translations.idiomatic: On renchen Liu Shouguang sent Wang Zunhua with a groveling letter; Dewei mocked him: "The Great Yan emperor has not even sacrificed at the suburbs—why so craven!

sentences.zh: 」守光再遣哀祈，德威乃以狀聞。

translations.literal: Shouguang again sent tearful pleas, and Dewei then reported it in a memorial.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang pleaded again, and Dewei forwarded the report.

sentences.zh: 己亥，劉光浚攻下平州，獲刺史張在吉。

translations.literal: On jihai Liu Guangjun took Ping prefecture and captured prefect Zhang Zaiji.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai Liu Guangjun seized Ping prefecture and took Prefect Zhang Zaiji.

sentences.zh: 五月壬寅朔，光浚進迫營州，刺史楊靖以城降。

translations.literal: Fifth month, first day renyin, Guangjun advanced on Ying prefecture; prefect Yang Jing surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On the renyin new moon of the fifth month Guangjun pressed Ying; Prefect Yang Jing yielded the city.

sentences.zh: 乙巳，梁將楊師厚會劉守奇率大軍侵鎮州。

translations.literal: On yisi Liang general Yang Shihou joined Liu Shouqi with a great army invading Zhen prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi Yang Shihou united with Liu Shouqi and invaded Zhen with a large force.

sentences.zh: 時帝之先鋒將史建瑭自趙州率五百騎入真定，師厚大掠鎮、冀之屬邑。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor's vanguard Shi Jiantang from Zhao prefecture led five hundred horse into Zhending; Shihou greatly plundered the subordinate counties of Zhen and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu's vanguard Shi Jiantang rode five hundred horse from Zhao into Zhending while Shihou ravaged the Zhen and Ji countryside.

sentences.zh: 王熔告急於周德威，德威分兵赴援，師厚移軍寇滄州，張萬進懼，遂降於梁。

translations.literal: Wang Rong reported urgency to Zhou Dewei; Dewei divided troops to go to the rescue; Shihou shifted the army to raid Cangzhou, and Zhang Wanjin in fear then surrendered to Liang.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong begged Zhou Dewei for help; Dewei detached a relief column; Shihou turned on Cangzhou, and a frightened Zhang Wanjin went over to Liang.

sentences.zh: 六月壬申朔，帝遣監軍張承業至幽州，與周德威會議軍事。

translations.literal: Sixth month, first day renshen, the Emperor sent supervising commissioner Zhang Chengye to Youzhou to confer on military affairs with Zhou Dewei.
translations.idiomatic: On the renshen new moon of the sixth month Cunxu sent Zhang Chengye to Youzhou to plan with Zhou Dewei.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，承業與德威率千騎至幽州西，守光遣人持信箭一隻，乞修和好。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Chengye and Dewei led a thousand horse west of Youzhou; Shouguang sent a man with one signal arrow begging to restore peace.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Chengye and Dewei took a thousand horse to the west of Youzhou; Shouguang sent a man with a single signal arrow suing for peace.

sentences.zh: 承業曰：「燕帥當令子弟一人為質則可。

translations.literal: Chengye said: "The Yan commander must send one son or younger brother as hostage—only then is it acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Chengye answered, "The Yan lord must leave a son or younger brother as hostage—only then."

sentences.zh: 」是日，燕將司全爽等十一人，並舉族來奔。

translations.literal: That day eleven Yan officers including Situ Quanshuang, each with their clans, came over.
translations.idiomatic: That same day eleven Yan officers led by Situ Quanshuang defected with their families.

sentences.zh: 辛亥，德威進攻諸城門。

translations.literal: On xinhai Dewei pressed the attack on the city gates.
translations.idiomatic: On xinhai Dewei assaulted the gates.

sentences.zh: 壬子，賊將楊師貴等五十人來降。

translations.literal: On renzi fifty rebel officers including Yang Shigui came to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi fifty enemy officers led by Yang Shigui surrendered.

sentences.zh: 甲子，五院軍使李信攻下莫州。

translations.literal: On jiazi Five-Courts Army commissioner Li Xin took Mo prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi Li Xin of the Five-Courts Army seized Mo prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時守光繼遣人乞降，將緩帝軍，陰令其將孟修、阮通謀於滄州節度使劉守奇，及求援於楊師厚，帝之遊騎擒其使以獻。

translations.literal: At that time Shouguang repeatedly sent men begging to surrender, intending to slow the Emperor's army; secretly he ordered his generals Meng Xiu and Ruan Tong to plot with Cangzhou military commissioner Liu Shouqi and also to seek aid from Yang Shihou—the Emperor's roaming scouts seized their envoys and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang kept suing to surrender to stall Cunxu while Meng Xiu and Ruan Tong secretly dealt with Liu Shouqi at Cangzhou and asked Yang Shihou for help—until Jin scouts seized the envoys and brought them in.

sentences.zh: 是月，帝會王鎔於天長。

translations.literal: That month the Emperor met Wang Rong at Tianchang.
translations.idiomatic: That month Cunxu met Wang Rong at Tianchang.

sentences.zh: 九月，劉守光率眾夜出，遂陷順州。

translations.literal: Ninth month, Liu Shouguang led his host out by night and thereupon took Shun prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Liu Shouguang sortied by night and seized Shun prefecture.

sentences.zh: 冬十月己巳朔，守光率七百騎、步軍五千夜入檀州。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, first day jisi, Shouguang with seven hundred horse and five thousand foot soldiers entered Tan prefecture by night.
translations.idiomatic: On the jisi new moon of the tenth month Shouguang slipped into Tan with seven hundred horse and five thousand foot.

sentences.zh: 庚午，周德威自涿州將兵躡之。

translations.literal: On gengwu Zhou Dewei led troops from Zhuozhou in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu Zhou Dewei marched from Zhuozhou in pursuit.

sentences.zh: 壬申，守光自檀州南山而遁，德威追及，大敗之，獲大將李劉、張景紹及將吏八百五十人，馬一百五十匹。

translations.literal: On renshen Shouguang fled south over the Tan hills; Dewei caught up, routed him, and took great generals Li Liu and Zhang Jingshao and more than eight hundred fifty officers and clerks, with one hundred fifty horses.
translations.idiomatic: On renshen Shouguang fled south over the Tan hills; Dewei overtook him, crushed his force, and captured the great generals Li Liu and Zhang Jingshao with eight hundred fifty officers and clerks and one hundred fifty horses.

sentences.zh: 守光得百餘騎遁入山谷，德威急馳，扼其城門，守光惟與親將李小喜等七騎奔入燕城。

translations.literal: Shouguang escaped into the valleys with a little over a hundred horse; Dewei galloped hard and seized the city gates; Shouguang with only his intimate officer Li Xiaoxi and six other horse rushed into the Yan capital.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang fled into the hills with barely a hundred riders; Dewei raced ahead and blocked the gates; Shouguang and seven intimates led by Li Xiaoxi alone broke into the Yan city.

sentences.zh: 己丑，守光遣牙將劉化修、周遵業等以書幣哀祈德威。

translations.literal: On jichou Shouguang sent tooth officers Liu Huaxiu and Zhou Zunye and others with letters and gifts in tearful plea to Dewei.
translations.idiomatic: On jichou he sent Liu Huaxiu, Zhou Zunye, and other staff with gifts and groveling letters to Dewei.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，守光乘城以病告，復令人獻自乘馬玉鞍勒易德威所乘馬而去，俄而劉光浚擒送守光偽殿直二十五人於軍門。

translations.literal: On gengyin Shouguang mounted the wall reporting illness; he again had a man present his own riding horse with jade saddle and bridle to exchange for the horse Dewei rode and leave; soon Liu Guangjun seized and sent twenty-five of Shouguang's false palace attendants to the army gate.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin he stood on the wall pleading sickness, then offered his own horse with jade trappings for Dewei's mount and withdrew; shortly Liu Guangjun delivered twenty-five of Shouguang's sham palace attendants to camp.

sentences.zh: 守光又乘城謂德威曰：「予俟晉王至，即泥首俟命。

translations.literal: Shouguang again mounted the wall and said to Dewei: "I shall wait until the Prince of Jin arrives, then smear my head in mud and await command.
translations.idiomatic: Shouguang called down again: "I will wait for the Prince of Jin, then kowtow and take orders."

sentences.zh: 」祈德威即馳驛以聞。

translations.literal: " He begged Dewei to gallop post-horses and report it.
translations.idiomatic: He urged Dewei to relay the plea by urgent dispatch.

sentences.zh: 十一月己亥朔，帝下令親征幽州。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, first day jihai, the Emperor ordered a personal campaign against Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the jihai new moon of the eleventh month Cunxu ordered a personal expedition to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 甲辰，發晉陽。

translations.literal: On jiachen he set out from Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiachen he left Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 己未，至范陽。

translations.literal: On jiwei he reached Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: On jiwei he arrived at Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，守光奉禮幣歸款於帝，帝單騎臨城邀守光，辭以他日，蓋為其親將李小喜所扼也。

translations.literal: On xinyou Shouguang presented ritual gifts and submitted; the Emperor alone rode to the wall to summon Shouguang, who declined for another day—because his intimate officer Li Xiaoxi held him in check.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou Shouguang offered ritual gifts and surrendered; Cunxu rode alone to the wall to call him out, but Shouguang put him off—Li Xiaoxi still had him in hand.

sentences.zh: 是夕，小喜來奔，帝下令諸軍，詰旦攻城。

translations.literal: That evening Xiaoxi came over; the Emperor ordered the armies to storm the city at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: That night Xiaoxi defected; Cunxu ordered an assault at dawn.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，梯童並進，軍士畢登，帝登燕丹塚以觀之。

translations.literal: On renxu scaling parties advanced together; the soldiers all mounted; the Emperor climbed the Yan Dan mound to watch.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu ladders went up together, the men scaled the walls, and Cunxu watched from the Yan Dan mound.

sentences.zh: 有頃，擒劉仁恭以獻。

translations.literal: Before long Liu Rengong was seized and presented.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Liu Rengong was captured and brought in.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，帝入燕城，諸將畢賀。

translations.literal: On guihai the Emperor entered the Yan capital; all the generals congratulated him.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai Cunxu entered the Yan city and the commanders hailed him.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚午，墨製授周德威幽州節度使。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, gengwu, by black-edict Zhou Dewei was made Youzhou military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: On gengwu in the twelfth month a black-edict made Zhou Dewei military commissioner of Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 癸酉，檀州燕樂縣人執劉守光並妻李氏祝氏、子繼祚以獻。

translations.literal: On guiyou the people of Yanle county in Tan prefecture seized Liu Shouguang together with his wife Lady Li, Lady Zhu, and son Jizuo and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: On guiyou men of Yanle in Tan seized Liu Shouguang with his wives Lady Li and Lady Zhu and his son Jizuo and delivered them.

sentences.zh: 己卯，帝下令班師，自雲、代而旋。

translations.literal: On jimao the Emperor ordered withdrawal of the army, returning by Yun and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: On jimao Cunxu ordered the host to withdraw by way of Yun and Dai.

sentences.zh: 時鎮州王鎔、定州王處直遣使請帝由井陘而西，許之。

translations.literal: At that time Zhen prefecture's Wang Rong and Ding prefecture's Wang Chuzhi sent envoys asking the Emperor to go west by Jingxing Pass; he agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Rong of Zhen and Wang Chuzhi of Ding asked him to return west through Jingxing, and he consented.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，帝發幽州，擄仁恭父子以行。

translations.literal: On gengchen the Emperor set out from Youzhou, taking Rengong and his son as captives.
translations.idiomatic: On gengchen he left Youzhou with Rengong and his son in bonds.

sentences.zh: 甲申，次定州，舍於關城。

translations.literal: On jiashen he halted at Ding prefecture and lodged at Guancheng.
translations.idiomatic: On jiashen he stopped at Ding and lodged at Guancheng.

sentences.zh: 翌日，次曲陽，與王處直謁北嶽祠。

translations.literal: Next day he halted at Quyang and with Wang Chuzhi paid respects at the North Peak temple.
translations.idiomatic: The next day he reached Quyang and with Wang Chuzhi worshipped at the North Peak shrine.

sentences.zh: 是日，次衡唐，鎮州王鎔迎謁於路。

translations.literal: That day he halted at Hengtang; Zhen prefecture's Wang Rong met and welcomed him on the road.
translations.idiomatic: That day he reached Hengtang, where Wang Rong met him on the road.

sentences.zh: 天祐十一年春正月戊戌朔，王鎔以履新之日，與其子昭祚、昭誨奉觴上壽置宴。

translations.literal: Spring of Tianyou 11, first month, first day wuxu, Wang Rong on the day of renewed shoes, with his sons Zhaozuo and Zhaohui, raised a cup, offered longevity wishes, and set a banquet.
translations.idiomatic: On the wuxu new moon of the first month of Tianyou 11 Wang Rong, on the day of new shoes, feasted Cunxu with his sons Zhaozuo and Zhaohui, toasting his long life.

sentences.zh: 鎔啟曰：「燕主劉太師頃為鄰國，今欲挹其風儀，可乎？

translations.literal: Rong opened and said: "Grand Tutor Liu of Yan was lately a neighboring state; now I wish to draw on his bearing—may I?
translations.idiomatic: Rong asked, "Grand Tutor Liu was our neighbor—may I meet the man?"

sentences.zh: 」帝即命主者破械，引仁恭、守光至，與之同宴，鎔饋以衣被飲食。

translations.literal: " The Emperor at once ordered the chief steward to break their fetters and led Rengong and Shouguang to the same banquet; Rong gave them clothing, bedding, food, and drink.
translations.idiomatic: Cunxu had their bonds struck off and brought Rengong and Shouguang to the table; Rong supplied them with clothes, bedding, food, and drink.

sentences.zh: 己亥，帝發鎮州，因與王鎔畋於衡唐之西。

translations.literal: On jihai the Emperor set out from Zhen prefecture and with Wang Rong hunted west of Hengtang.
translations.idiomatic: On jihai he left Zhen and hunted west of Hengtang with Wang Rong.

sentences.zh: 壬子，至晉陽，以組練繫仁恭、守光，號令而入。

translations.literal: On renzi he reached Jinyang, bound Rengong and Shouguang with silken cords, and entered at the command.
translations.idiomatic: On renzi he reached Jinyang, led Rengong and Shouguang in with silken bonds, and entered in state.

sentences.zh: 是日，誅守光。

translations.literal: That day Shouguang was executed.
translations.idiomatic: That day Shouguang was put to death.

sentences.zh: 遣大將李存霸拘送仁恭於代州，刺其心血奠告於武皇陵，然後斬之。

translations.literal: A great general, Li Cunba, was sent to escort Rengong under guard to Dai prefecture, pierce his heart-blood and offer it in report at Wuhuang's tomb, and then behead him.
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunba escorted Rengong to Dai, pierced his heart and offered the blood at Wuhuang's tomb, then struck off his head.

sentences.zh: 是月，鎮州王鎔、定州王處直遣使推帝為尚書令。

translations.literal: That month Zhen prefecture's Wang Rong and Ding prefecture's Wang Chuzhi sent envoys urging the Emperor as Director-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: That month Wang Rong and Wang Chuzhi sent envoys urging Cunxu to accept the post of Director-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 初，王鎔稱藩於梁，梁以鎔為尚書令，至是鎮、定以帝南破梁軍，北定幽、薊，乃共推崇焉。

translations.literal: Earlier Wang Rong had submitted as a vassal to Liang, and Liang made Rong Director-in-Chief; now Zhen and Ding, because the Emperor had broken Liang armies in the south and settled You and Ji in the north, together promoted him.
translations.idiomatic: Rong had once bowed to Liang and been made Director-in-Chief; now Zhen and Ding, after Cunxu's southern victories and northern pacification, jointly pressed the title on him.

sentences.zh: 使三至，帝讓乃從之，遂選日受冊，開霸府，建行台，如武德故事。

translations.literal: Envoys came thrice; the Emperor declined until he followed; he then chose a day to receive the investiture, opened a hegemon's bureau, and established a field headquarters on the Wude model.
translations.idiomatic: Three embassies came before he yielded; he chose a day for the rite, opened a hegemon's office, and set up a field headquarters after the Wude precedent.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，帝親將自黃沙嶺東下會鎮人，進軍邢、洺。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, the Emperor personally led troops east down from Huangshaling to join the Zhen men, advancing on Xing and Ming.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Cunxu marched in person east from Huangshaling to join the Zhen army and advanced on Xing and Ming.

sentences.zh: 梁將楊師厚軍於漳東，帝軍次張公橋，既而裨將曹進金奔於梁，帝軍不利而退。

translations.literal: Liang general Yang Shihou was encamped east of Zhang; the Emperor's army halted at Zhanggong Bridge; before long staff officer Cao Jinjing defected to Liang; the Emperor's army met with ill fortune and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shihou held the east bank of the Zhang; Cunxu camped at Zhanggong Bridge until staff officer Cao Jinjing went over to Liang; the Jin host faltered and pulled back.

sentences.zh: 八月，還晉陽。

translations.literal: Eighth month, he returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he returned to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 天祐十二年三月，梁魏博節度使賀德倫遣使奉幣乞盟。

translations.literal: Third month of Tianyou 12, Liang Weibo military commissioner He Delun sent envoys with gifts begging alliance.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of Tianyou 12 He Delun of Weibo sent envoys with gifts to sue for peace.

sentences.zh: 時楊師厚卒於魏州，梁主乃割相、衛、澶三州別為一鎮，以德倫為魏博節度使，以張筠為相州節度使，魏人不從。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Shihou died at Weizhou; the Liang Founder then carved out Xiang, Wei, and Chan as a separate commandery, made Delun military commissioner of Weibo, and Zhang Jun military commissioner of Xiang—but the Wei men would not obey.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Shihou had just died at Weizhou; the Liang Founder split Xiang, Wei, and Chan into a separate circuit, made Delun commissioner of Weibo and Zhang Jun commissioner of Xiang, and the Wei troops refused to submit.

sentences.zh: 是月二十九日夜，魏軍作亂，囚德倫於牙署，三軍大掠。

translations.literal: On the night of the twenty-ninth of that month the Wei army mutinied, imprisoned Delun in the headquarters, and the three armies plundered on a great scale.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-ninth night of that month the Wei army mutinied, locked Delun in headquarters, and the host looted the city.

sentences.zh: 軍士有張彥者，素實凶暴，為亂軍之首，迫德倫上章請卻復六州之地，梁主不從，遂迫德倫歸於帝，且乞師為援。

translations.literal: Among the soldiers was one Zhang Yan, by nature fierce and brutal, leader of the mutineers; he forced Delun to memorialize asking restoration of the six prefectures; the Liang Founder would not agree, so he forced Delun to the Emperor and also begged troops as relief.
translations.idiomatic: A soldier named Zhang Yan, brutal by nature, led the mutiny; he made Delun petition for the six prefectures back, and when the Liang Founder refused he drove Delun to the Emperor and asked for an army.

sentences.zh: 帝命馬步副總管李存審自趙州帥師屯臨清，帝自晉陽東下，與存審會。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Li Cunshen, deputy overall commander of horse and foot, to lead troops from Zhao prefecture and camp at Linqing; the Emperor himself marched east from Jinyang and joined Cunshen.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor ordered Li Cunshen from Zhao to camp at Linqing and marched east from Jinyang to join him.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《通鑒》：晉王引大軍自黃澤嶺東下，與存審會於臨清，猶疑魏人之詐，按兵不進。）〉

translations.literal: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: The Prince of Jin led a great army east down from Huangze Ridge, joined Cunshen at Linqing, still suspected Wei deceit, and held the army without advancing.)〉
translations.idiomatic: (The 《Zizhi Tongjian》 says: The Prince of Jin came east from Huangze Ridge, met Cunshen at Linqing, still distrusted the Wei men, and would not advance.)〉

sentences.zh: 賀德倫遣從事司空頲至軍，密啟張彥狂勃之狀，且曰：「若不剪此亂階，恐貽後悔。

translations.literal: He Delun sent his aide Sikong Yan to the army in secret, reporting Zhang Yan's violent insolence, and saying: "If this source of disorder is not cut off, I fear later regret.
translations.idiomatic: Delun sent his aide Sikong Yan in secret to report Zhang Yan's violence and say, "Unless this trouble is rooted out, we will regret it.

sentences.zh: 」帝默然，遂進軍永濟。

translations.literal: " The Emperor was silent and then advanced the army to Yongji.
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said nothing and marched on Yongji.

sentences.zh: 張彥謁見，以銀槍效節五百人從，皆被甲持兵以自衛。

translations.literal: Zhang Yan came to an audience with five hundred Silver Spear oath-bound men following, all in armor and bearing arms to guard themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan came to audience with five hundred Silver Spear guards in armor, weapons in hand.

sentences.zh: 帝登樓諭之曰：「汝等在城，濫殺平人，奪其妻女，數日以來，迎訴者甚眾，當斬汝等，以謝鄴人。

translations.literal: The Emperor ascended a tower and addressed them: "You in the city slaughtered common people at will and seized their wives and daughters; for days petitions have been many—you should be beheaded to answer the people of Ye."
translations.idiomatic: From a tower the Emperor told them: "You butchered civilians and seized their women; for days the complaints have poured in—you should die to answer Ye."

sentences.zh: 」遽令斬彥及同惡者七人，軍士股栗，帝親加慰撫而退。

translations.literal: He at once ordered Yan and seven fellow villains beheaded; the soldiers trembled in their legs; the Emperor personally comforted them and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: He had Yan and seven ringleaders cut down at once; the troops shook with fear; then he soothed them and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 翌日，帝輕裘緩策而進，令張彥部下軍士被甲持兵，環馬而從，命為帳前銀槍，眾心大服。

translations.literal: The next day the Emperor advanced in light fur and loose reins; he had Zhang Yan's men don armor and weapons, ring his horse, and named them Silver Spears before the tent—the host's hearts were greatly won.
translations.idiomatic: Next day he rode forward in light dress, had Yan's men arm and ring his horse, made them his Silver Spears before the tent, and won the army over.

sentences.zh: 梁將鄩聞帝至，以精兵萬人自洹水趣魏縣，帝命李存審帥師禦之，帝率親軍於魏縣西北，夾河為柵。

translations.literal: The Liang general Liu Xun, hearing the Emperor had arrived, led ten thousand elite troops from Huanshui toward Weixian; the Emperor ordered Li Cunshen to lead troops to meet him while he himself with the personal guard camped northwest of Weixian, palisades on both banks of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Liu Xun, hearing the Emperor was near, took ten thousand picked men from Huanshui toward Weixian; the Emperor sent Cunshen to block him and camped his guard northwest of the city, palisading both banks.

sentences.zh: 六月庚寅朔，帝入魏州，賀德倫上符印，請帝兼領魏州，帝從之。

translations.literal: Sixth month, first day gengyin, the Emperor entered Weizhou; He Delun presented his tallies and seals and asked that the Emperor also hold Weizhou—the Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: On gengyin, the first of the sixth month, he entered Weizhou; Delun handed over his seals and asked him to take the circuit, and he agreed.

sentences.zh: 墨製授德倫大同軍節度，令取便路赴任。

translations.literal: By ink edict Delun was made military commissioner of Datong and ordered to take the convenient road to his post.
translations.idiomatic: An ink edict made Delun commissioner of Datong and sent him to his post by the nearest road.

sentences.zh: 帝下令撫諭鄴人，軍城畏肅，民心大服。

translations.literal: The Emperor issued orders to comfort the people of Ye; the army city was awed into discipline and popular hearts were greatly won.
translations.idiomatic: He issued orders to reassure Ye; discipline returned to the garrison and the people submitted.

sentences.zh: 是時，以貝州張源德據壘拒命；

translations.literal: At that time Zhang Yuande of Bei prefecture held a stockade and refused orders;
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yuande of Bei still held a fort and would not obey;

sentences.zh: 南通劉鄩，又與滄州首尾相應，聞德州無備，遣別將襲之，遂拔其城。

translations.literal: to the south he was in contact with Liu Xun and coordinated with Cangzhou; hearing Dezhou was undefended, he sent a separate commander to raid it and took the city.
translations.idiomatic: he was tied to Liu Xun in the south and to Cangzhou; learning Dezhou was undefended, he sent a detachment and took it.

sentences.zh: 命遼州牙將馬通為德州刺史，以扼滄、貝之路。

translations.literal: and the Emperor appointed Ma Tong, a Ya officer of Liaozhou, military commissioner of Dezhou to choke the Cang and Bei routes.
translations.idiomatic: and the Emperor made Ma Tong of Liaozhou commissioner of De to block Cang and Bei.

sentences.zh: 秋七月，梁澶州刺史王彥章棄城而遁，畏帝軍之逼也。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, Liang Chanzhou prefect Wang Yanzhang abandoned the city and fled, fearing the press of the Emperor's army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wang Yanzhang of Chan abandoned his city and fled before the Jin host.

sentences.zh: 以故將李岩為澶州刺史。

translations.literal: The former general Li Yan was made Chanzhou prefect.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yan, a former officer, was made prefect of Chan.

sentences.zh: 帝至魏縣，因率百餘騎覘梁軍之營。

translations.literal: When the Emperor reached Weixian he led a little more than a hundred horse to reconnoiter the Liang camp.
translations.idiomatic: At Weixian he rode out with a little over a hundred men to scout the Liang camp.

sentences.zh: 是日陰晦，劉鄩伏兵五千於河南叢木間。

translations.literal: That day was overcast; Liu Xun had five thousand ambush troops in the wooded thickets south of the river.
translations.idiomatic: The day was dark; Liu Xun had five thousand men in ambush among the trees south of the river.

sentences.zh: 帝至，伏兵忽起，大噪而來，圍帝數十重。

translations.literal: When the Emperor arrived the ambush suddenly rose, shouting loudly as they came, and surrounded him several tens deep.
translations.idiomatic: When the Emperor came up the ambush burst out with a roar and ringed him many ranks deep.

sentences.zh: 帝以百騎馳突奮擊，梁軍辟易，決圍而出。

translations.literal: The Emperor with a hundred horse charged and fought fiercely; the Liang army gave way; he broke the encirclement and came out.
translations.idiomatic: He charged with his hundred horse, the Liang line split, and he broke out.

sentences.zh: 有頃，援軍至，乃解。

translations.literal: Before long relief troops arrived and he was freed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon reinforcements came and he was safe.

sentences.zh: 帝顧謂軍士曰：「幾為賊所笑。」

translations.literal: The Emperor looked back and told the soldiers: "I was nearly laughed at by the bandits."
translations.idiomatic: He told his men, "The enemy nearly made a fool of me."

sentences.zh: 是月，劉鄩潛師由黃澤西趨晉陽，至樂平而還，遂軍於宗城。

translations.literal: That month Liu Xun led troops in secret by Huangze west toward Jinyang; he reached Leping and returned, then encamped at Zongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: That month Liu Xun stole west by Huangze toward Taiyuan, turned back at Leping, and camped at Zongcheng.

sentences.zh: 初，鄩在洹水，數日不出，寂無聲跡。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Xun was at Huanshui he did not come out for days; there was silence and no sign.
translations.idiomatic: While Xun lay at Huanshui he stayed quiet for days without a sound.

sentences.zh: 帝遣騎覘之，無斥候者，城中亦無煙火之狀，但有鳥止於壘上，時見旗幟循堞往來。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent horse to scout; there were no outposts; within the city too there was no smoke or fire—only birds perched on the ramparts, and now and then banners moving along the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Scouts found no pickets and no smoke in the town—only birds on the walls and banners now and then along the parapet.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「我聞劉鄩用兵，一步百變，必以詭計誤我。

translations.literal: The Emperor said: "I have heard Liu Xun in warfare changes a hundred paces at once—he must use a trick to mislead me."
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, "Liu Xun changes his moves every step—he must be tricking us."

sentences.zh: 」使視城中，乃縛旗於芻偶之上，使驢負之，循堞而行。

translations.literal: He had the city inspected—it was straw dummies with flags bound on them, donkeys carrying them along the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Inside were straw figures with flags, carried by donkeys along the wall.

sentences.zh: 得城中羸老者詰之，雲軍去已二日矣。

translations.literal: They seized old and weak men in the city and questioned them; they said the army had been gone two days.
translations.idiomatic: Old men in the city said the army had left two days before.

sentences.zh: 既而有人自鄩軍至者，言兵已趨黃澤，帝遽發騎追之。

translations.literal: Then someone came from Xun's army saying the troops had already hurried toward Huangze; the Emperor at once sent horse in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: A man from Xun's camp said they were already on Huangze; the Emperor sent cavalry after them at once.

sentences.zh: 時霖雨積旬，鄩軍倍道兼行，皆腹疾足腫，加以山路險阻，崖穀泥滑，緣蘿引葛，方得少進。

translations.literal: Rain had fallen for more than ten days; Xun's army marched day and night together; all suffered belly ailments and swollen feet; added to that the mountain roads were perilous, cliffs and ravines muddy and slippery—they pulled vines and creepers and only then could advance a little.
translations.idiomatic: After weeks of rain Xun's men forced the march with belly sickness and swollen feet on muddy cliffs, hauling themselves along by vines.

sentences.zh: 顛墜岩阪，陷於泥淖而死者十二三。

translations.literal: Those who tumbled from cliffs and banks and sank in mud and mire died one or two in ten.
translations.idiomatic: One or two in ten died falling from cliffs or drowning in the mud.

sentences.zh: 前軍至樂平，糗糒將竭，聞帝軍追躡於後，太原之眾在前，群情大駭。

translations.literal: The van reached Leping; dry rations were nearly exhausted; hearing the Emperor's army pursuing from behind and Taiyuan's masses ahead, every heart was greatly terrified.
translations.idiomatic: The van reached Leping with rations almost gone; Jin pursuit behind and Taiyuan ahead, the host panicked.

sentences.zh: 鄩收合其眾還，自邢州陳宋口渡漳水而東，駐於宗城。

translations.literal: Xun gathered his host and returned, crossed the Zhang River east from Chen Song Ford in Xingzhou, and halted at Zongcheng.
translations.idiomatic: Xun turned back, crossed the Zhang east from Chen Song Ford, and camped at Zongcheng.

sentences.zh: 時魏之軍儲已乏，臨清積粟所在，鄩欲引軍據之。

translations.literal: By then Wei's military stores were exhausted; grain was piled at Linqing, and Xun wished to lead the army to seize it.
translations.idiomatic: Wei stores were empty and grain lay at Linqing; Xun meant to seize it.

sentences.zh: 周德威初聞鄩軍之西，自幽州率千騎至土門。

translations.literal: When Zhou Dewei first heard Xun's army had gone west, he led a thousand horse from Youzhou to Tumen.
translations.idiomatic: When Dewei first heard Xun had gone west, he raced a thousand horse from Youzhou to Tumen.

sentences.zh: 及鄩軍東下，急趨南宮，知鄩軍在宗城，遣十餘騎迫其營，擒斥候者，斷其腕，令還。

translations.literal: When Xun's army marched east he hurried to Nangong; learning Xun was at Zongcheng he sent a dozen horse to press his camp, seized scouts, cut off their wrists, and sent them back.
translations.idiomatic: When Xun turned east Dewei rushed to Nangong, found him at Zongcheng, seized scouts, cut off their wrists, and sent them back.

sentences.zh: 德威至臨清，鄩起軍駐貝州。

translations.literal: Dewei reached Linqing; Xun raised camp and halted at Bei prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei reached Linqing; Xun broke camp and held Bei.

sentences.zh: 帝率親騎次博州，鄩軍於堂邑，周德威自臨清率五百騎躡之。

translations.literal: The Emperor led personal horse to Bo prefecture; Xun's army was at Tangyi; Zhou Dewei from Linqing led five hundred horse in pursuit.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor camped near Bo while Xun was at Tangyi; Dewei from Linqing followed with five hundred horse.

sentences.zh: 是日，鄩軍於莘縣，帝營於莘西一舍，城壘相望，日夕交鬥。

translations.literal: That day Xun's army was at Shen county; the Emperor camped one stage west of Shen; ramparts faced each other and they fought at dusk every day.
translations.idiomatic: Xun lay at Shen; the Emperor camped a stage west; the camps faced each other and skirmished every evening.

sentences.zh: 八月，梁將賀瑰襲取澶州，帝遣李存審率兵五千攻貝州，因塹而圍之。

translations.literal: Eighth month, the Liang general He Gui seized Chanzhou; the Emperor sent Li Cunshen with five thousand troops to attack Bei prefecture and besieged it behind trenches.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month He Gui took Chan; the Emperor sent Cunshen with five thousand to trench and besiege Bei.

sentences.zh: 冬十月，有軍士自鄩軍來奔，帝善待之，乃劉鄩密令齎鴆賂帝膳夫，欲置毒於食中，會有告者，索其黨誅之。

translations.literal: Winter, tenth month, a soldier deserted from Xun's army; the Emperor treated him well; it turned out Liu Xun had secretly sent him bearing poison to bribe the Emperor's cooks, intending to put poison in the food; there was an informer; his accomplices were sought out and executed.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of winter a deserter from Xun was well treated and revealed a plot to poison the Emperor's food; the men involved were seized and killed.

sentences.zh: 天祐十三年春二月，帝知劉鄩將謀速戰，乃聲言歸晉陽以誘之，實勞軍於貝州也；

translations.literal: Second month of spring in Tianyou 13, the Emperor knew Liu Xun would plan a quick battle; he proclaimed return to Jinyang to lure him while actually resting the army at Bei;
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tianyou 13, knowing Xun wanted a quick fight, he announced a return to Taiyuan but rested his army at Bei;

sentences.zh: 令李存審守其營。

translations.literal: he ordered Li Cunshen to hold the camp.
translations.idiomatic: he left Cunshen to hold the camp.

sentences.zh: 鄩謂帝已臨晉陽，將乘虛襲鄴。

translations.literal: Xun thought the Emperor had already reached Jinyang and meant to strike Ye while it was empty.
translations.idiomatic: Xun thought the Emperor was in Taiyuan and meant to strike empty Ye.

sentences.zh: 三月，鄩遣其將楊延直自澶州率兵萬人，會於城下。

translations.literal: Third month, Xun sent his general Yang Yanzhi from Chanzhou with ten thousand troops to join below the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month Xun sent Yang Yanzhi from Chan with ten thousand men to the walls.

sentences.zh: 夜半，至於南門之外。

translations.literal: At midnight they reached outside the south gate.
translations.idiomatic: At midnight they reached the south gate.

sentences.zh: 城中潛出壯士五百人，突入延直之軍，噪聲動地，梁軍自亂。

translations.literal: Five hundred stalwart men slipped out of the city, burst into Yanzhi's army, and the noise shook the earth; the Liang army fell into disorder of itself.
translations.idiomatic: Five hundred men slipped out, struck Yanzhi's camp, and the Liang line collapsed in uproar.

sentences.zh: 遲明，鄩自莘引軍至城東，與延直兵會。

translations.literal: At dawn Xun led troops from Shen to the east of the city and joined Yanzhi's force.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn Xun came from Shen to the east wall and joined Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 鄩之來也，李存審率兵踵其後，李嗣源自魏城出戰。

translations.literal: As Xun came, Li Cunshen followed with troops from behind; Li Siyuan came out to fight from Weicheng.
translations.idiomatic: Cunshen followed Xun's rear while Li Siyuan sallied from Weicheng.

sentences.zh: 俄而帝自貝州至，鄩卒見帝，驚曰：「晉王耶！

translations.literal: Before long the Emperor arrived from Bei prefecture; Xun's soldiers on seeing the Emperor cried in alarm: "The Prince of Jin!
translations.idiomatic: Soon the Emperor came from Bei; Xun's men cried, "The Prince of Jin!

sentences.zh: 」因引軍漸卻，至故元城西，李存審大軍已成列矣。

translations.literal: " They then drew the army back step by step to the old Yuancheng west wall; Li Cunshen's great army was already formed in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: " and fell back to old Yuancheng; Cunshen's main host was already in line.

sentences.zh: 軍前後為方陣，梁軍於其間為圓陣，四面受敵。

translations.literal: Front and rear were square formations; the Liang army between them was a circular formation, attacked on four sides.
translations.idiomatic: Jin lines square before and behind penned the Liang circle on every side.

sentences.zh: 兩軍初合，梁軍稍衄；

translations.literal: When the two armies first joined, the Liang army was slightly checked;
translations.idiomatic: At the first clash the Liang line buckled;

sentences.zh: 再合，鄩引騎軍突西南而走。

translations.literal: on the second clash Xun led horse to burst southwest and flee.
translations.idiomatic: on the second, Xun broke southwest with his horse.

sentences.zh: 帝以騎軍追擊之，梁步兵合戰，短兵既接，帝軍鼓噪，圍之數重，埃塵漲天。

translations.literal: The Emperor with cavalry pursued; the Liang infantry joined battle; once short weapons met the Emperor's army shouted and surrounded them several layers deep; dust billowed to the sky.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor chased with horse while the Liang foot fought; at close quarters the Jin host roared in and ringed them until dust blotted the sky.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源以千騎突入其間，眾皆披靡，相躪如積。

translations.literal: Li Siyuan with a thousand horse burst into their midst; all were routed and trampled one upon another like heaps.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan drove a thousand horse into them; men were crushed in heaps.

sentences.zh: 帝軍四面斬擊，棄甲之聲，聞數十里。

translations.literal: The Emperor's army slashed on four sides; the sound of cast-off armor was heard for several tens of li.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin host cut them down on every side; discarded armor clattered for miles.

sentences.zh: 眾既奔潰，帝之騎軍追及於河上，十百為群，赴水而死，梁步兵七萬殲亡殆盡。

translations.literal: Once the masses had broken and fled, the Emperor's cavalry pursued to the river; in groups of tens and hundreds they threw themselves into the water and died; the Liang foot army of seventy thousand was annihilated nearly to the last man.
translations.idiomatic: The rout ran to the river in clusters of ten and hundred and drowned; seventy thousand Liang foot were almost wiped out.

sentences.zh: 劉鄩自黎陽濟，奔滑州。

translations.literal: Liu Xun crossed from Liyang and fled to Hua prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Xun crossed from Liyang and fled to Hua.

sentences.zh: 是月，梁主遣別將王檀率兵五萬，自陰地關趨晉陽，急攻其城，昭義李嗣昭遣將石嘉才率騎三百赴援。

translations.literal: That month the Liang Founder sent a separate commander Wang Tan with fifty thousand troops from Yindi Pass toward Jinyang in a rush to storm the city; Zhaoyi Li Sizhao sent his commander Shi Jiacai with three hundred horse as relief.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Liang Founder sent Wang Tan with fifty thousand from Yindi Pass to storm Taiyuan; Li Sizhao sent Shi Jiacai with three hundred horse.

sentences.zh: 時安金全、張承業堅守於內，嘉才救援於外，檀懼，乃燒營而遁，追擊至陰地關。

translations.literal: An Jinquan and Zhang Chengye held firm within while Jiacai relieved from without; Tan was afraid, burned camp and fled, and pursuit reached Yindi Pass.
translations.idiomatic: An Jinquan and Zhang Chengye held the city while Jiacai struck from outside; Tan burned his camp and fled to Yindi Pass.

sentences.zh: 時鄩敗於莘縣，王檀遁於晉陽，梁主聞之，曰：「吾事去矣！

translations.literal: By then Xun had been defeated at Shen county and Wang Tan had fled from Jinyang; the Liang Founder heard it and said: "My cause is lost!
translations.idiomatic: When news came of Xun's defeat at Shen and Tan's flight from Taiyuan, the Liang Founder said, "My cause is lost!

sentences.zh: 」三月乙卯朔，分兵以攻衛州。

translations.literal: " On the first day yimao of the third month he divided troops to attack Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: " On yimao in the third month he sent troops against Wei prefecture.

sentences.zh: 壬戌，刺史米昭以城降。

translations.literal: On renxu prefect Mi Zhao surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu Mi Zhao surrendered Wei.

sentences.zh: 夏四月，攻洺州，下之。

translations.literal: Summer, fourth month, they attacked Luozhou and took it.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month they took Luo.

sentences.zh: 五月，帝還晉陽。

translations.literal: Fifth month, the Emperor returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month the Emperor returned to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 六月，命偏師攻閻寶於邢州，梁主遣捉生都將張溫率步騎五百為援，至內黃，溫率眾來奔。

translations.literal: Sixth month, he ordered a detached force to attack Yan Bao at Xingzhou; the Liang Founder sent Life-Capture chief Zhang Wen with five hundred foot and horse as relief; at Neihuang Wen led the masses to defect.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month a column besieged Yan Bao at Xing; the Liang Founder sent Zhang Wen with five hundred men, but Wen defected with his troops at Neihuang.

sentences.zh: 秋七月甲寅朔，帝自晉陽至魏州。

translations.literal: Autumn, seventh month, first day jiayin, the Emperor came from Jinyang to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: On jiayin, the first of the seventh month, he came from Taiyuan to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 八月，大閱師徒，進攻邢州。

translations.literal: Eighth month, he reviewed the army and advanced to attack Xingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month he reviewed the host and besieged Xing.

sentences.zh: 相州節度使張筠棄城遁去，以袁建豐為相州刺史，依舊隸魏州。

translations.literal: Xiangzhou military commissioner Zhang Jun abandoned the city and fled; Yuan Jianfeng was made Xiang prefect and remained subordinate to Weizhou as before.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun of Xiang fled; Yuan Jianfeng became prefect of Xiang under Weizhou again.

sentences.zh: 邢州節度使閻寶請以城降，以忻州刺史、蕃漢副總管李存審為邢州節度使，以閻寶為西南面招討使，遙領天平軍節度使。

translations.literal: Xingzhou military commissioner Yan Bao asked to surrender the city; Xinzhou prefect and Han-Tang deputy overall commander Li Cunshen was made Xing military commissioner, Yan Bao made southwest campaign commissioner and titular military commissioner of Tianping.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Bao of Xing offered surrender; Cunshen of Xin became commissioner of Xing, and Bao became southwest campaign commander with a nominal Tianping commission.

sentences.zh: 是月，契丹入蔚州，振武節度使李嗣本陷於契丹。

translations.literal: That month the Khitan entered Wei prefecture; Zhenwu military commissioner Li Siben fell into Khitan hands.
translations.idiomatic: That month the Khitan took Wei; Li Siben of Zhenwu was captured.

sentences.zh: 九月，帝還晉陽。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the Emperor returned to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he returned to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 梁滄州節度使戴思遠棄城遁去，舊將毛璋入據其城。

translations.literal: Liang Cangzhou military commissioner Dai Siyuan abandoned the city and fled; the old officer Mao Zhang entered and held it.
translations.idiomatic: Dai Siyuan of Cang fled; Mao Zhang, an old officer, seized the city.

sentences.zh: 李嗣源帥師招撫，璋以城降。

translations.literal: Li Siyuan led troops to win them over; Zhang surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: Li Siyuan marched to win them; Zhang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 乃以李存審為滄州節度使，以李嗣源為邢州節度使。

translations.literal: Then Li Cunshen was made Cangzhou military commissioner and Li Siyuan Xing military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Cunshen became commissioner of Cang and Siyuan commissioner of Xing.

sentences.zh: 時契丹犯塞，帝領親軍北征，至代州北，聞蔚州陷，乃班師。

translations.literal: At that time the Khitan raided the frontier; the Emperor led the personal guard north; reaching north of Daizhou he heard Wei had fallen and turned the army back.
translations.idiomatic: When the Khitan raided the border he marched north with his guard; north of Dai he heard Wei had fallen and turned back.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《遼史·太祖紀》：十一月，攻蔚、新、武、媯、儒五州，自代北至河曲，逾陰山，盡有其地。

translations.literal: (The 《History of the Liao · Annals of the Taizu》: Eleventh month, he attacked Wei, Xin, Wu, Ji, and Ru—five prefectures—from north of Dai to Hequ, crossed Yin Mountain, and held all that land.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《History of the Liao · Annals of the Taizu》: In the eleventh month he took Wei, Xin, Wu, Ji, and Ru from north of Dai to Hequ, crossed Yin Mountain, and held the whole region.

sentences.zh: 其圍蔚州，敵樓無故自壞，眾軍大噪，乘之，不逾時而破。）〉

translations.literal: In besieging Wei the enemy tower broke for no reason; the host shouted greatly and pressed; in less than an hour it fell.)〉
translations.idiomatic: At Wei the watchtower collapsed without cause; the army roared and stormed the place and took it in less than an hour.)〉

sentences.zh: 是月，貝州平，以滄州降將毛璋為貝州刺史。

translations.literal: That month Bei prefecture was pacified; Mao Zhang, the Cangzhou defector, was made Bei prefect.
translations.idiomatic: That month Bei fell; Mao Zhang, who had come over from Cang, was made prefect of Bei.

sentences.zh: 自是，河朔悉為帝所有。

translations.literal: From this the whole Hebei region belonged to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: From then on all Hebei was his.

sentences.zh: 帝自晉陽復至於魏州。

translations.literal: The Emperor came again from Jinyang to Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He returned from Taiyuan to Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 天祐十四年二月，帝聞劉鄩復收殘兵保守黎陽，遂率師以攻之，不克而還。

translations.literal: Second month of Tianyou 14, the Emperor heard Liu Xun had again gathered remnant troops to hold Liyang; he led troops to attack but could not take it and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of Tianyou 14, hearing Xun had rallied at Liyang, he attacked, failed, and withdrew.

sentences.zh: 是月甲午，新州將盧文進殺節度使李存矩，叛入契丹，遂引契丹之眾寇新州。

translations.literal: That month on jiawu Xinzhou commander Lu Wenjin killed military commissioner Li Cunju, rebelled into the Khitan, and led Khitan troops to raid Xin.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu that month Lu Wenjin of Xin killed commissioner Li Cunju, went over to the Khitan, and led them against Xin.

sentences.zh: 存矩，帝之諸弟也，治民失政，禦下無恩，故及於禍。

translations.literal: Cunju was the Emperor's younger brother; in governing the people his policy failed and in commanding subordinates he showed no kindness—therefore he met calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Cunju was the Emperor's brother; he ruled badly and treated his men harshly, and so came to ruin.

sentences.zh: 帝以契丹主安巴堅與武皇屢盟於雲中，既又約為兄弟，急難相救，至是容納叛將，違盟犯塞，乃馳書以讓之。

translations.literal: The Emperor, because the Khitan ruler Abaoji with Wuhuang had often sworn alliance at Yunzhong and afterward also agreed to be brothers, aiding each other in urgent peril—now harboring a defector, breaking alliance and raiding the frontier—hurriedly sent a letter to reproach him.
translations.idiomatic: Abaoji had sworn brotherhood with Wuhuang at Yunzhong and pledged mutual aid; now sheltering a traitor and breaking the pact, the Emperor sent a sharp letter of reproach.

sentences.zh: 契丹攻新州甚急，刺史安金全棄城而遁，契丹以文進部將劉殷為刺史。

translations.literal: The Khitan attacked Xin with great urgency; prefect An Jinquan abandoned the city and fled; the Khitan made Wenjin's officer Liu Yin prefect.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan stormed Xin; An Jinquan fled; they made Wenjin's man Liu Yin prefect.

sentences.zh: 帝命周德威率兵三萬攻之，營於城東。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Zhou Dewei with thirty thousand troops to attack; he camped east of the city.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor sent Zhou Dewei with thirty thousand to besiege Xin and camped east of the walls.

sentences.zh: 俄而文進引契丹大至，德威拔營而歸，因為契丹追躡，師徒多喪。

translations.literal: Before long Wenjin led a great Khitan host; Dewei broke camp and returned, was pursued by the Khitan, and many of the army were lost.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin soon brought a great Khitan host; Dewei broke camp, was chased home, and lost many men.

sentences.zh: 契丹乘勝寇幽州。

translations.literal: The Khitan pressed the victory and raided Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan pressed on to raid Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 是時言契丹者，或云五十萬，或云百萬，漁陽以北，山谷之間，氈車毳幕，羊馬彌漫。

translations.literal: At that time those who spoke of the Khitan said either five hundred thousand or a million; north of Yuyang, between mountains and valleys, felt carts and felt tents, sheep and horses, spread without end.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors put the Khitan at five hundred thousand or a million; north of Yuyang carts and tents and herds filled every valley.

sentences.zh: 盧文進招誘幽州亡命之人，教契丹為攻城之具，飛梯、衝車之類，畢陳於城下。

translations.literal: Lu Wenjin recruited Youzhou men in exile and taught the Khitan siege engines—flying ladders, battering rams, and the like—all arrayed below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: Wenjin gathered Youzhou exiles and taught the Khitan ladders, rams, and every siege device below the walls.

sentences.zh: 鑿地道，起土山，四面攻城，半月之間，機變百端，城中隨機以應之，僅得保全，軍民困弊，上下恐懼。

translations.literal: They dug tunnels, raised earthen hills, and attacked on four sides; within half a month stratagems changed a hundred ways; the city answered each move as it came and barely held; army and people were worn, high and low were afraid.
translations.idiomatic: They tunneled, heaped earth, and assaulted from every side; for half a month tricks multiplied and the city barely held; soldiers and civilians were spent and terrified.

sentences.zh: 德威間道馳使以聞，帝憂形於色，召諸將會議。

translations.literal: Dewei sent a messenger by a hidden route in haste to report; worry showed on the Emperor's face and he summoned the generals to council.
translations.idiomatic: Dewei sent word by a hidden path; the Emperor's face showed worry and he called his generals to council.

sentences.zh: 時李存審請急救燕、薊，且曰：「我若猶豫，未行，但恐城中生事！

translations.literal: At that time Li Cunshen asked for urgent relief of Yan and Ji, and said: "If I hesitate and do not march, I fear only that trouble will arise in the city!
translations.idiomatic: Li Cunshen then begged for swift relief of Yan and Ji, saying, "If I hold back and do not go, the city may revolt before we arrive!

sentences.zh: 」李嗣源曰：「願假臣突騎五千，以破契丹。

translations.literal: " Li Siyuan said: "I beg leave to borrow five thousand shock cavalry to break the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: " Li Siyuan said, "Give me five thousand shock horse and I will break the Khitan."

sentences.zh: 」閻寶曰：「但當搜選銳兵，控製山險，強弓勁弩，設伏待之。

translations.literal: " Yan Bao said: "One need only search out and select sharp troops, control the mountain defiles, deploy strong bows and powerful crossbows, and set ambushes to await them.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan Bao said, "Pick the best troops, hold the passes, post strong bows and crossbows, and lie in wait."

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「吾有三將，無復憂矣！」

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "I have three generals—no more worries!"
translations.idiomatic: " The Emperor said, "With these three commanders I need not worry again!"

sentences.zh: 夏四月，命李嗣源率師赴援，次於淶水；

translations.literal: Fourth month of summer, the Emperor ordered Li Siyuan to lead troops to the relief and encamped at the Lai River;
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth month of summer he sent Li Siyuan to the rescue; Siyuan halted at the Lai River;

sentences.zh: 又遣閻寶率師夜過祁溝，俘擒而還。

translations.literal: He also sent Yan Bao with troops by night across Qigou, captured prisoners, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: and sent Yan Bao by night through Qigou to seize prisoners and withdraw.

sentences.zh: 周德威遣人告李嗣源曰：「契丹三十萬，馬牛不知其數，近日所食羊馬過半，阿保機責讓盧文進，深悔其來。

translations.literal: Zhou Dewei sent word to Li Siyuan: "The Khitan are three hundred thousand; horses and cattle beyond counting; of late they have consumed more than half their sheep and horses. Abaoji reprimanded Lu Wenjin and deeply regrets having come.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Dewei reported to Li Siyuan: "The Khitan number three hundred thousand, with herds beyond count; they have already eaten more than half their sheep and horses. Abaoji blames Lu Wenjin and bitterly regrets this campaign.

sentences.zh: 契丹勝兵散布射獵，安巴堅帳前不滿萬人，宜夜出奇兵，掩其不備。

translations.literal: Their elite troops are scattered hunting; fewer than ten thousand remain before An Bojian's tent. By night send picked troops to surprise them unprepared.
translations.idiomatic: Their best men are out hunting; fewer than ten thousand guard the ruler's tent at An Bojian. Strike by night while they are off guard.

sentences.zh: 」嗣源具以事聞。

translations.literal: " Siyuan reported the matter in full.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan sent the full report to court.

translations.literal: 〈Bracket note
translations.idiomatic: 〈Note

sentences.zh: （《遼史·太祖紀》：四月，圍幽州，不克。

translations.literal: (The 《History of the Liao》, “Basic Annals of the Founder”: In the fourth month they besieged Youzhou but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: (The 《History of the Liao》, “Basic Annals of the Founder”: In the fourth month they invested Youzhou without success.

sentences.zh: 六月乙巳，望城中有氣如煙火狀，上曰：「未可攻也。

translations.literal: On yisi in the sixth month, seeing qi in the city like smoke and fire, the ruler said: "It cannot yet be attacked.
translations.idiomatic: On yisi in the sixth month, seeing vapors over the city like smoke and flame, the Khitan ruler said, "Do not attack yet.

sentences.zh: 」以大暑霖潦，班師，留盧國用守之。

translations.literal: " Because of great summer rains and floods, he withdrew the army and left Lu Guoyong to hold it.
translations.idiomatic: " In the heavy summer rains he withdrew, leaving Lu Guoyong to garrison the place.

sentences.zh: 是契丹主已於六月退師矣。）〉

translations.literal: By then the Khitan ruler had already withdrawn in the sixth month.)〉
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan ruler had in fact already withdrawn that sixth month.)〉

sentences.zh: 秋七月辛未，帝遣李存審領軍與嗣源會於易州，步騎凡七萬。

translations.literal: Seventh month, day xinwei, the Emperor sent Li Cunshen with an army to join Siyuan at Yizhou; foot and horse together totaled seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: On xinwei in the seventh month the Emperor sent Li Cunshen to join Siyuan at Yizhou with seventy thousand foot and horse.

sentences.zh: 於是三將同謀，銜枚束甲，尋澗穀而行，直抵幽州。

translations.literal: Then the three generals joined counsel, gagged their mouths and bound their armor, marched along streams and valleys, and went straight to Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The three commanders then marched in silence with armor bound, following ravines straight to Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 八月甲午，自易州北循山而行，李嗣源率三千騎為前鋒。

translations.literal: Eighth month, day jiawu, from Yizhou north along the mountains; Li Siyuan led three thousand cavalry as vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On jiawu in the eighth month they left Yizhou north along the hills; Li Siyuan led three thousand horse in the van.

sentences.zh: 庚子，循大房嶺而東，距幽州六十里。

translations.literal: Day gengzi, they followed Dafang Ridge east, sixty li from Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On gengzi they turned along Dafang Ridge, sixty li from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 契丹萬騎遽至，存審、嗣源極力以拒之，契丹大敗，委棄毳幕、氈廬、弓矢、羊馬不可勝紀，進軍追討，俘斬萬計。

translations.literal: Khitan ten thousand horse came suddenly; Cunshen and Siyuan resisted with all their strength; the Khitan were greatly defeated, abandoning felt tents, felt huts, bows, sheep, and horses beyond reckoning; the advancing army pursued, and captives and heads numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Ten thousand Khitan horse rushed up; Cunshen and Siyuan met them head-on and routed them, leaving felt tents, huts, bows, and countless sheep and horses; the pursuit took tens of thousands of heads and prisoners.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，大軍入幽州，德威見諸將，握手流涕。

translations.literal: Day xinchou, the great army entered Youzhou; Dewei saw the generals, took their hands, and wept.
translations.idiomatic: On xinchou the main force entered Youzhou; Dewei clasped the generals' hands and wept.

sentences.zh: 翌日，獻捷於鄴。

translations.literal: The next day he presented the victory report at Ye.
translations.idiomatic: The next day the victory was reported at Ye.

sentences.zh: 九月，班師，帝授存審檢校太傅，嗣源檢校太保，閻寶加同平章事。

translations.literal: Ninth month, the army returned; the Emperor made Cunshen acting Grand Tutor, Siyuan acting Grand Guardian, and added Yan Bao as Tongping Grand Councilor.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month they withdrew; Cunshen was made acting Grand Tutor, Siyuan acting Grand Guardian, and Yan Bao was added Tongping Grand Councilor.

sentences.zh: 十月，帝自魏州還晉陽。

translations.literal: Tenth month, the Emperor returned from Weizhou to Jinyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the Emperor went from Weizhou back to Jinyang.

sentences.zh: 十一月，復至魏州。

translations.literal: Eleventh month, he again reached Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month he was at Weizhou again.

sentences.zh: 十二月，帝觀兵於河上。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, the Emperor reviewed troops on the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he reviewed the army on the Yellow River.

sentences.zh: 時梁人據楊劉城，列柵相望，帝率軍履河冰而渡，盡平諸柵，進攻楊劉城。

translations.literal: At that time the Liang held Yangliu city, palisades in rows facing one another; the Emperor led the army treading river ice to cross, leveled all the palisades, and advanced to attack Yangliu.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang held Yangliu with facing stockades; the Emperor crossed on the ice, tore down every palisade, and besieged Yangliu.

sentences.zh: 城中守兵三千人，帝率騎軍環城馳射，又令步兵持斧斬其鹿角，負葭葦以堙塹；

translations.literal: The garrison was three thousand; the Emperor led cavalry circling the city shooting arrows, and also ordered infantry with axes to cut the deer-horn stakes and carry rushes to fill the ditch;
translations.idiomatic: Three thousand men defended the city; he rode around it shooting, and ordered foot soldiers to cut the abatis, heap rushes into the ditch,

sentences.zh: 帝自負一圍而進，諸軍鼓噪而登，遂拔其壘，獲守將安彥之。

translations.literal: The Emperor himself carried one bundle of encircling material and advanced; the armies shouted and climbed; they then took the fortress and captured the defender An Yanzhi.
translations.idiomatic: then shouldered a bundle of fascines himself and went forward; the host stormed the wall, took the fort, and seized An Yanzhi.

sentences.zh: 是夕，帝宿楊劉。

translations.literal: That evening the Emperor lodged at Yangliu.
translations.idiomatic: That night he camped at Yangliu.

sentences.zh: 天祐十五年春正月，帝軍徇地至鄆、濮。

translations.literal: Spring, first month of Tianyou 15, the Emperor's army raided territory as far as Yan and Pu.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of spring, Tianyou 15, he raided through Yan and Pu.

sentences.zh: 時梁主在洛，將修郊禮，聞楊劉失守，狼狽而還。

translations.literal: The Liang ruler was at Luoyang about to perform the suburban sacrifice; hearing Yangliu had fallen, he returned in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ruler was at Luoyang preparing the suburban rites; when Yangliu fell he hurried back in disarray.

sentences.zh: 二月，梁將謝彥章帥眾數萬來迫楊劉，築壘以自固，又決河水，彌漫數里，以限帝軍。

translations.literal: Second month, Liang general Xie Yanzhang led tens of thousands pressing Yangliu, built camps to fortify himself, and also broke the river banks so the water spread for several li to hem in the Emperor's army.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month Xie Yanzhang of Liang brought tens of thousands against Yangliu, entrenched, and breached the dykes until the flood spread for li to block the Jin host.

sentences.zh: 六月壬戌，帝自魏州復至楊劉。

translations.literal: Sixth month, day renxu, the Emperor from Weizhou again reached Yangliu.
translations.idiomatic: On renxu in the sixth month he returned from Weizhou to Yangliu.

sentences.zh: 甲子，率諸軍涉水而進，梁人臨水拒戰，帝軍小卻。

translations.literal: Day jiazi, he led the armies wading forward; the Liang resisted at the water and the Emperor's army slightly withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he forded forward; the Liang met him in the stream and the Jin line briefly gave ground.

sentences.zh: 俄而鼓噪復進，梁軍漸退，因乘勢而擊之。

translations.literal: Soon drums and shouts advanced again; the Liang army gradually retreated, and he therefore took the opportunity to strike.
translations.idiomatic: Then the drums sounded and the Jin surged again; the Liang fell back and he pressed the attack.

sentences.zh: 交鬥於中流，梁軍大敗，殺傷甚眾，河水如絳，謝彥章僅得免去。

translations.literal: They fought in midstream; the Liang army was greatly defeated, killed and wounded very many, the river like crimson; Xie Yanzhang barely escaped.
translations.idiomatic: They grappled in midstream; the Liang were shattered with heavy losses and the water ran red; Xie Yanzhang alone got away.

sentences.zh: 是月，淮南楊溥遣使來會兵，將致討於梁也。

translations.literal: That month Yang Pu of Huainan sent envoys to join armies, intending to campaign against Liang.
translations.idiomatic: That month Yang Pu of Huainan sent envoys to combine forces for a strike on Liang.

sentences.zh: 秋八月辛丑朔，大閱於魏郊，河東、魏博、幽、滄、鎮定、邢洺、麟、勝、雲、朔十鎮之師，及奚、契丹、室韋、吐渾之眾十餘萬，部陣嚴肅，旌甲照曜，師旅之盛，近代為最。

translations.literal: Autumn, eighth month, new moon xinchou, a great review at the Wei outskirts: armies of the ten commands—Hedong, Weibo, You, Cang, Zhen-Ding, Xing-Mo, Lin, Sheng, Yun, and Shuo—and masses of Xi, Khitan, Shiwei, and Tuhun numbering more than one hundred thousand; formations were strict, banners and armor dazzling; in recent times no host had been so grand.
translations.idiomatic: On the xinchou new moon in the eighth month he held a grand review outside Wei: the ten commands—Hedong, Weibo, You, Cang, Zhen-Ding, Xing-Mo, Lin, Sheng, Yun, and Shuo—with Xi, Khitan, Shiwei, and Tuhun, over a hundred thousand in all, drawn up in glittering array, the finest host of the age.

sentences.zh: 己酉，梁兗州節度使張萬進遣使歸款。

translations.literal: Day jiyou, Liang Yanzhou military commissioner Zhang Wanjin sent envoys to submit.
translations.idiomatic: On jiyou Zhang Wanjin, Liang commissioner of Yanzhou, sent envoys to surrender.

sentences.zh: 帝自魏州率師次於楊劉，略地至鄆、濮而還；

translations.literal: The Emperor from Weizhou led the army to halt at Yangliu, raided territory to Yan and Pu and returned;
translations.idiomatic: From Weizhou he marched to Yangliu, raided Yan and Pu, and came back;

sentences.zh: 遂營於麻家渡，諸陣列營十數。

translations.literal: He then encamped at Majia Ford with more than ten formations in line.
translations.idiomatic: then camped at Majia Ford with a dozen separate lines.

sentences.zh: 梁將賀瑰、謝彥章以軍屯濮州行台村，結壘相持百餘日。

translations.literal: Liang generals He Gui and Xie Yanzhang with the army encamped at Xingtai Village in Puzhou, building camps and facing one another for more than a hundred days.
translations.idiomatic: He Gui and Xie Yanzhang of Liang lay at Xingtai Village in Pu with facing camps for over a hundred days.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗以數百騎摩壘求戰，謝彥章率精兵五千伏於堤下，帝以十餘騎登堤，伏兵發，圍帝十數重。

translations.literal: The Emperor once with several hundred cavalry brushed the palisades seeking battle; Xie Yanzhang led five thousand elite troops lying in ambush below the dyke; the Emperor with a dozen horsemen mounted the dyke; the ambush sprang and surrounded the Emperor more than ten layers deep.
translations.idiomatic: Once he rode out with a few hundred horse to provoke a fight; Xie Yanzhang hid five thousand picked men below the embankment; the Emperor climbed the dyke with a dozen riders and was ringed ten deep.

sentences.zh: 俄而帝之騎軍繼至，攻於圍外，帝於圍中躍馬奮擊，決圍而出。

translations.literal: Soon the Emperor's cavalry followed; they attacked outside the ring; within the ring the Emperor leaped his horse and struck fiercely, breaking out of the encirclement.
translations.idiomatic: His cavalry soon came up and struck from outside while he fought within and broke free.

sentences.zh: 李存審兵至，梁軍方退。

translations.literal: Li Cunshen's troops arrived and only then did the Liang army withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Cunshen arrived the Liang finally drew off.

sentences.zh: 是時，帝銳於接戰，每馳騎出營，存審必扣馬進諫，帝伺存審有間，即策馬而出，顧左右曰：「老子妨吾戲耳！

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor was keen for close combat; whenever he galloped from camp Cunshen would seize his bridle and remonstrate; the Emperor watched for an opening in Cunshen's attention and would spur out, turning to his attendants and saying: "The old man is spoiling my sport!
translations.idiomatic: He was eager for hand-to-hand fighting and often dashed from camp; Cunshen always caught his bridle to warn him, so he waited until Cunshen's guard slipped, then spurred out and told his attendants, "The old fellow is ruining my fun!

sentences.zh: 」至是幾危，方以存審之言為忠也。

translations.literal: " On this occasion he was nearly lost, and only then took Cunshen's words as loyal.
translations.idiomatic: " This time he nearly died and at last saw that Cunshen had been faithful.

sentences.zh: 十二月庚子朔，帝進軍，距梁軍柵十里而止。

translations.literal: Twelfth month, new moon gengzi, the Emperor advanced; he halted ten li from the Liang palisades.
translations.idiomatic: On the gengzi new moon in the twelfth month he marched forward and stopped ten li from the Liang lines.

sentences.zh: 時梁將賀瑰殺騎將謝彥章於軍，帝聞之曰：「賊帥自相魚肉，安得不亡。

translations.literal: At that time Liang general He Gui killed cavalry commander Xie Yanzhang in the army; hearing it the Emperor said: "The enemy leaders are devouring one another—how can they not perish?
translations.idiomatic: He Gui of Liang had just killed his cavalry commander Xie Yanzhang in camp; the Emperor said, "Their chiefs are butchering each other—how can they stand?

sentences.zh: 」戊午，下令軍中老幼，令歸魏州，悉兵以趣汴。

translations.literal: " On wuwu he ordered the army's old and young to return to Weizhou and massed all troops to press Bian.
translations.idiomatic: " On wuwu he sent the army's families back to Weizhou and drove every fighting man toward Bian.

sentences.zh: 庚申，大軍毀營而進。

translations.literal: On gengshen the great army broke camp and advanced.
translations.idiomatic: On gengshen the host struck camp and marched.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，次於臨濮，梁軍舍營踵於後。

translations.literal: On xinyou they halted at Linpu; the Liang army abandoned camp and followed behind.
translations.idiomatic: On xinyou they reached Linpu with the Liang trailing behind.

sentences.zh: 癸亥，次胡柳坡。

translations.literal: On guihai they halted at Huliu Slope.
translations.idiomatic: On guihai they camped at Huliu Slope.

sentences.zh: 遲明，梁軍亦至，帝率親軍出視，諸軍從之。

translations.literal: At dawn the Liang army also arrived; the Emperor led the personal guard out to reconnoiter and the armies followed.
translations.idiomatic: At first light the Liang came up; he rode out with his guard to look and the whole army followed.

sentences.zh: 梁軍已成陣，橫亙數十里，帝亦以橫陣抗之。

translations.literal: The Liang army had already formed its battle line, stretching across several tens of li; the Emperor also opposed them with a transverse formation.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang were already drawn up for tens of li; he answered with a line across their front.

sentences.zh: 時帝與李存審總河東、魏博之眾居其中，周德威以幽、薊之師當其西，鎮、定之師當其東。

translations.literal: At that time the Emperor with Li Cunshen commanded the Hedong and Weibo masses in the center; Zhou Dewei with the You and Ji troops faced their west; the Zhen and Ding troops faced their east.
translations.idiomatic: He and Li Cunshen held Hedong and Weibo in the center; Zhou Dewei took You and Ji on the west; Zhen and Ding faced the east.

sentences.zh: 梁將賀瑰、王彥章全軍接戰，帝以銀槍軍突入梁軍陣中，斬擊十餘里，賀瑰、王彥章單騎走濮陽。

translations.literal: Liang generals He Gui and Wang Yanzhang joined battle with their full armies; the Emperor's Silver Spear Army burst into the Liang line, cutting for more than ten li; He Gui and Wang Yanzhang fled alone on horseback to Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: He Gui and Wang Yanzhang of Liang met him with their whole force; the Silver Spear Army pierced the Liang array for more than ten li and He Gui and Wang Yanzhang rode alone to Puyang.

sentences.zh: 帝軍輜重在陣西，望見梁軍旗幟，皆驚走，因自相蹈籍，不能禁止。

translations.literal: The Emperor's baggage was west of the line; seeing Liang banners, all panicked and fled, trampling one another so that none could be stopped.
