translations.idiomatic: Jin baggage lay west of the field; at sight of Liang flags the train stampeded and could not be checked.

sentences.zh: 帝一軍先敗，周德威戰歿。

translations.literal: The Emperor's wing was first defeated; Zhou Dewei died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His own wing broke first and Zhou Dewei fell in the rout.

sentences.zh: 是時，陂中有土山，梁軍數萬先據之，帝帥中軍至山下。

translations.literal: At that time in the slope was an earthen hill; tens of thousands of Liang troops had already seized it; the Emperor led the central army to the foot of the hill.
translations.idiomatic: A hill rose in the hollow; tens of thousands of Liang had seized it first and he brought the center to its foot.

sentences.zh: 梁軍嚴整不動，旗幟甚盛。

translations.literal: The Liang army was drawn up rigid and unmoving, banners very grand.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang ranks stood firm, their banners towering.

sentences.zh: 帝呼諸軍曰：「今日之戰，得山者勝。

translations.literal: The Emperor called to the armies: "In today's battle, whoever holds the hill wins.
translations.idiomatic: He shouted to his men, "Whoever holds that hill wins today.

sentences.zh: 賊已據山，吾與爾等各馳一騎以奪之！

translations.literal: The bandits already hold the hill—we and you each charge one horse to seize it!
translations.idiomatic: The enemy already have it—charge with me, each man one horse!"

sentences.zh: 」帝率軍先登，銀槍步兵繼進，遂奪其山。

translations.literal: The Emperor led the army up first; Silver Spear foot soldiers followed; they then seized the hill.
translations.idiomatic: He led the climb and the Silver Spear foot came after; the hill was theirs.

sentences.zh: 梁軍紛紜而下，復於土山西結陣數里。

translations.literal: The Liang army poured down in disorder and again formed a line several li west of the hill.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang tumbled down in confusion and re-formed several li west of the hill.

sentences.zh: 時日已晡矣，或曰：「諸軍未齊，不如還營，詰朝可圖再戰。

translations.literal: The sun was already past the hour of shen; someone said: "The armies are not yet all assembled—better return to camp and fight again at dawn.
translations.idiomatic: It was already late afternoon when someone urged, "Not all our units are up—withdraw to camp and fight again tomorrow.

sentences.zh: 」閻寶曰：「深入賊境，逢其大敵，期於盡銳，以決雌雄。

translations.literal: " Yan Bao said: "Deep in enemy territory we have met their main force; the time is set to spend every man and decide the issue.
translations.idiomatic: " Yan Bao said, "We are deep in enemy country facing their main host; this is the hour to stake everything.

sentences.zh: 況賊帥奔亡，眾心方恐，今乘高擊下，勢如破竹矣！

translations.literal: Moreover their commander has fled and their hearts are afraid; now strike from the height and the momentum will be like splitting bamboo!
translations.idiomatic: Their chief has run and their hearts are shaken; strike downhill and we will cut them like bamboo!"

sentences.zh: 」銀槍都將王建及被甲橫槊進曰：「賊將先已奔亡，王之騎軍一無所損，賊眾晡晚，大半思歸，擊之必破。

translations.literal: Silver Spear commander Wang Jianji, armored and with level spear, advanced and said: "The enemy commander has already fled; Your Majesty's cavalry are unharmed; most of the enemy masses at evening think of returning—strike them and they will surely break.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Jianji of the Silver Spear, in armor with spear level, stepped forward: "Their general has fled and your horse are untouched; by evening most of the Liang want home—hit them and they will shatter.

sentences.zh: 王但登山縱觀，責臣以破賊之效。

translations.literal: Your Majesty need only climb the hill and watch; charge me with the merit of breaking the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Mount the hill and look on; hold me to account for breaking them."

sentences.zh: 」於是李嗣昭領騎軍自土山北以逼梁軍，王建及呼土眾曰：「今日所失輜重，並在山下。

translations.literal: Thereupon Li Sizhao led cavalry from north of the hill to press the Liang army; Wang Jianji called to the men on the hill: "Today's lost baggage is all below the hill.
translations.idiomatic: Li Sizhao then led horse from the north of the hill against the Liang; Wang Jianji shouted to the troops on the height, "All the baggage we lost today lies below!

sentences.zh: 」乃大呼以奮擊，諸軍繼之，梁軍大敗。

translations.literal: " He then shouted and struck fiercely; the armies followed; the Liang army was greatly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: " and led a roaring charge; the rest poured after and the Liang were routed.

sentences.zh: 時元城令吳瓊、貴鄉令胡裝各部役徒萬人，於山下曳柴揚塵，鼓噪助其勢。

translations.literal: At that time Yuancheng magistrate Wu Qiong and Guixiang magistrate Hu Zhuang each led ten thousand corvée laborers below the hill dragging brush and raising dust, drumming and shouting to aid the momentum.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Qiong of Yuancheng and Hu Zhuang of Guixiang each brought ten thousand laborers to drag brush, raise dust, and drum and shout to swell the din.

sentences.zh: 梁軍不之測，自相騰籍，棄甲山積。

translations.literal: The Liang army could not fathom it; they trampled one another in panic, abandoning armor in mountains of piles.
translations.idiomatic: The Liang could not tell what was happening; they stampeded and cast off armor in heaps.

sentences.zh: 甲子，命行戰場，收獲鎧仗不知其數。

translations.literal: Day jiazi, he ordered traversal of the battlefield; captured armor and weapons were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: On jiazi he swept the field and the captured arms were beyond count.

sentences.zh: 時帝之軍士有先入大梁問其次舍者，梁人大恐，驅市人以守。

translations.literal: At that time some of the Emperor's soldiers had already entered Daliang to ask after their lodgings; the Liang were greatly afraid and drove market people to defend.
translations.idiomatic: Some Jin soldiers had already gone into Daliang to ask where they might lodge; the Liang were terrified and pressed townsfolk into defense.

sentences.zh: 其殘眾奔歸汴者不滿千人，帝軍遂拔濮陽。

translations.literal: Their remnant masses fleeing back to Bian numbered fewer than a thousand; the Emperor's army then took Puyang.
translations.idiomatic: Fewer than a thousand Liang survivors reached Bian; the Jin host then took Puyang.
